contracts.declared_mechanism: @landlock_tool decorator factory wrapping sync tool functions (rejecting coroutines), spawning a forkserver/spawn-context child running _child_main, which reinstalls the parent config singleton and calls _apply_landlock_rules: Ruleset.allow(...) per allowed path followed by rs.apply(); require_sandbox (default true per config.py:103-105) turns child-side ImportError/RuntimeError into an error payload the parent re-raises; init_sandbox_mp_context('forkserver') is initialized at startup after fail-closed diagnostics (main.py:144-157).
contracts.forbidden_condition: A @landlock_tool-wrapped tool function reaching filesystem access outside a Landlock-confined child: execution in the parent process (e.g., via TRASHDIG_SKIP_SANDBOX=1), on a non-Linux platform where Landlock is a no-op, or in a child where ruleset application failed while require_sandbox=true and the call nevertheless proceeds unsandboxed.

contracts.protected_operation: Invocation of tool functions wrapped by @landlock_tool (e.g., read_file(file_path, ...)): the wrapper resolves config in the parent, strips tool-context kwargs, spawns a child via SandboxProvider.mp_context.Process(target=_child_main) (landlock_tool.py:428-447), and the child runs the tool body only after Landlock is applied (landlock_tool.py:313-315).
contracts.protected_resource: The host filesystem outside the allowed set: workspace root (read-only unless write=True), caller-declared extra read-only paths, Python runtime prefixes and sys.path snapshot, /proc/self, /tmp (scratch access), /dev (read-only).
contracts.protection_obligation: Every tool function registered under the @landlock_tool decorator (e.g., read_file) must execute only inside a spawned child process whose filesystem access is confined by an irreversibly applied Landlock ruleset — workspace root read-only by default (read+write only when write=True), declared extra paths and Python runtime/sys.path entries read-only, /proc/self read-only, /tmp scratch-writable, /dev read-only — and, when require_sandbox=true (the configuration default), any failure to apply Landlock on Linux must abort the tool call rather than fall through to unsandboxed execution.
scope_limits: Landlock enforcement is Linux-only; on non-Linux platforms the child runs with an unrestricted filesystem (landlock_tool.py:15-16, 290-292, 339-342).

TRASHDIG_SKIP_SANDBOX=1 bypasses the child process entirely and executes the tool in-process (landlock_tool.py:17-18, 409-411); the source labels this a test-suite path but no production guard against setting it is visible.
When require_sandbox=false, Landlock import/application failure degrades to a logged warning and unsandboxed execution inside the child (landlock_tool.py:295-311).
The ruleset confines the filesystem only; no network or other access domain is restricted by this mechanism (landlock_tool.py:171-218).

Access inside the allowed set is permitted by design: workspace read-only unless write=True (landlock_tool.py:187-189, 361-363), /tmp scratch-writable (lines 210-212), /dev read-only (lines 214-216), extra_paths read-only (lines 191-194).
Coverage is limited to functions decorated with @landlock_tool; tools decorated only with @artifact_tool (e.g., container_bash_tool) are outside this mechanism.
The wrapper strips only tool_context/ctx kwargs (landlock_tool.py:423-426); all other caller-supplied arguments are pickled into the child.

If Docker is unavailable, the tool raises under require_sandbox=true (unless TRASHDIG_SKIP_SANDBOX=1), but otherwise falls back to host bash_tool execution (container_bash_tool.py:56-66); the image allowlist gates entry to the tool body but does not meaningfully constrain that host fallback.
container_bash_tool is not wrapped by @landlock_tool; its isolation is the Docker invocation itself (--network none, read-only workspace mount) at container_bash_tool.py:72-86.
